correctness.rationale: Frozen proof line 71 reverses the signs of the two plateaux; the replacement RESULT.md fixes this without changing the correct exponent pair or the theorem. Independently, |r|≤1 and the all-interval averages on diverging hostile and favorable plateaux are respectively −1 and +1, so both extreme Bohl exponents are attained in the long-interval definition. The positive invariant interval gives y=1/p and y′=−ry+2. Each reflected ramp has exactly zero net integral and contributes an additive integral between 2η exp(−η) and 2η exp(η). Propagating hostile, first ramp, favorable, final ramp gives y_{n+1}=q_n y_n+b_n with q_n=e^(H_n−F_n), b_n=2q_n(1−e^(−H_n))+2(1−e^(−F_n))+e^(−F_n)B_n+E_n. Thus q_n→q=e^(−δ) and b_n→2(1+q). Eventual contraction gives the affine limiting fixed point if q<1; eventual expansion gives y_n→∞ if q>1. If q=1, for each h>0 small one eventually has y_{n+1}≥(1−h)y_n+3, hence liminf y_n≥3/h and y_n→∞. At each hostile finish p≤e^(−H_n); from the next ramp to the favorable start p remains o(1), then increases on the favorable plateau while p<1/2. The last ramp changes p by at most 3η_n, giving the stated full-time peak as the limit of the season boundaries. For the specified balanced calendar b_n−4 is absolutely summable and q_n=1 exactly, giving y_n=4n+O(1) and n p(T_n)→1/4. The source checker was inspected, not run.
